---
title: "7.6 Sensitivity and stress"
order: 6
---

Early Warning has two kinds of setting a validator would move: the two tier cutoffs, which
training sets, and the trigger thresholds, which policy sets. This page records what the
committed facts already show about each, and says plainly what has **not been run**. No
scenario on this page is invented: where a sensitivity was not computed, the page says so and
carries it to the monitoring plan or the next redevelopment.

## Tier cutoffs

**What the facts show.** The cutoffs' largest sensitivity is not to a small move in their
value but to the rows they are taken over. Taken over the whole book, mostly in-sample
probabilities, they put {{< var ews.tier.High.share >}} of the book in the High tier and
{{< var ews.tier_ho.High.share >}} of held-out accounts there
([7.4](assumptions.qmd#ews-tiers-as-a-fixed-mix)). That difference, a PSI of
{{< var ews.tier_ho.psi_vs_book >}} over the three tiers, dwarfs anything a modest move of
either cutoff would do, and it is the evidence for finding 1 ([7.7](limitations.qmd)).

**Not run.**

- *Moving either cutoff by a fixed step* and re-tiering the held-out accounts. Adjudication's
  equivalent is in D5.6; no such scenario is computed for Early Warning.
- *Cutoffs taken from out-of-sample probabilities* — the quantiles of held-out or
  cross-validated probabilities, which is the control finding 1 proposes. Its effect on the
  tier mix and on the High tier's capture is unmeasured until the next retrain.

The v2 workbench lets a reviewer move either cutoff and see the whole book re-tiered, through
the same `risk_tier` the batch uses ([7.1](purpose.qmd#who-consumes-it-and-how)). It is the tool
for exploring a cutoff; it re-tiers the whole book, in-sample rows included, so it shows the
workload a cutoff gives on the book, not on new accounts.

## Trigger thresholds

**What the facts show.** Two statements follow from the facts without a scenario, because a
threshold above a feature's largest value can never be crossed:

- **The `DELINQUENCY` rule's configured threshold has no effect anywhere above the data.**
  `dpd_max` never exceeds {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.feature_max >}} over
  the book, so `dpd_severe` could move from {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.threshold >}}
  to any value above that maximum without changing a single flag. The trigger's behaviour is
  set entirely by the hard-coded `dpd_recent` clause, which the configuration cannot reach
  (finding 6).
- **`DEPOSIT_DECLINE` sits near the edge of its data.** Its threshold,
  {{< var ews.trigger.deposit_decline.clause.deposit_decline_pct.threshold >}}, is close to the
  largest decline in the book, {{< var ews.trigger.deposit_decline.clause.deposit_decline_pct.feature_max >}};
  it fires on {{< var ews.trigger.deposit_decline.n >}} accounts, and any threshold above that
  maximum silences it.

For the other triggers the facts give each one's firing count alone
([7.4](assumptions.qmd#ews-trigger-thresholds-are-generic)) and its precision and recall
([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-trigger-performance)), at the committed threshold only.

**Not run.** A sweep of any threshold — the fire rate, precision and recall as each moves —
is not computed. It is the evidence finding 7's control needs, and is carried there and to the
monitoring plan ([7.8](monitoring.qmd)). The workbench lets a reviewer move every
configured threshold and see the book's trigger counts change, through the same
`flag_triggers` the batch uses; it does not show precision, and it cannot move the hard-coded
`dpd_recent` clause.

## Sampling sensitivity of the gate

The one stress the facts do run on the model is the bootstrap of the held-out accounts
([7.5](performance.qmd#how-firm-each-result-is)): {{< var ews.boot.capture_below_gate >}} of
resamples fall below the capture gate. That is a sensitivity of the gate's *verdict* to the
sample, not of the model to its inputs, and it is finding 3.

## Reduced-input refits: not run

D4 refits the scorecard on reduced inputs (D4.6). No such refit is run for Early Warning.
What can be said without one:

- **The score reaches this model directly.** `pd_score` alone ranks the held-out accounts
  about as well as the model ([7.5](performance.qmd#ews-benchmark)); a model refitted without
  the score has not been measured, and is the experiment finding 4 asks for.
- **A missing panel is not an alert.** If an account's monthly history were missing, the
  left join in `compute_ews_features` would leave its panel features empty, and they would
  become zero: no utilisation, no drift, no days past due, no overdrafts. Zero fires no
  trigger — that much follows from `flag_triggers` with the committed thresholds, where every rule needs a value above a
  positive threshold or above zero. What the model's probability would be for such an account
  has not been computed. The generated data have a full panel for every account, so neither is
  exercised ([7.7](limitations.qmd#ews-observations)).

Both refits — without the score, and without the panel, with an account missing its history
referred rather than scored — are listed for the next redevelopment
([7.8](monitoring.qmd#ews-redevelopment-triggers)).
